questions.question: Gharana Parampara is found in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustani Classical Music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• The term **Gharana** refers to a system of social organization linking musicians or dancers by lineage or apprenticeship.
 
• In Hindustani Classical Music, Gharanas represent schools or traditions of music, each with its distinct style and techniques.
 
• Some well-known Hindustani Gharanas include **Gwalior, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, and Kirana**.
 
• The Gharana system became prominent during the Mughal period, where court musicians passed on their skills to disciples or family members.
 
• Each Gharana has unique characteristics in terms of raga rendition, ornamentation, and improvisation techniques, contributing to the diversity of Hindustani Classical Music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following acts was passed during the period of Viceroy Dufferin?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Indian Telegraph Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Telegraph Act** was passed during the tenure of **Viceroy Lord Dufferin** (1884-1888).
 
• This act provided the **legal framework for telecommunication systems** in India.
 
• It gave the **Government of India exclusive rights** to establish, maintain, and regulate telecommunication systems in the country.
 
• The act has been amended multiple times to accommodate modern communication technologies, including the **internet and mobile services**.
 
• It also contains provisions that allow the government to **intercept communications** for reasons such as national security, public safety, or prevention of crime.
 
• The act laid the foundation for the development of **telecommunication infrastructure** in colonial and post-colonial India.
 
• Lord Dufferin played a significant role in the **administrative and infrastructural modernization** of India during his tenure as Viceroy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ilbert Bill**__
 __
 
• The **Ilbert Bill** was introduced in 1883 during the tenure of **Lord Ripon**, not Lord Dufferin.
 
• It sought to allow Indian judges to try British offenders in criminal cases in district courts.
 
• The bill faced strong opposition from the European community in India and was eventually amended, limiting its scope.
 
• The controversy surrounding the bill highlighted the **racial discrimination** prevalent in colonial India.
 
 
 
• **Age of Consent Act**__
 __
 
• This act was passed in **1891** during the tenure of **Lord Lansdowne**.
 
• It aimed to raise the minimum age of consent for marriage for girls to **12 years**.
 
• The act was a response to growing concerns about **child marriage** and its impact on the health and well-being of young girls.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act**__
 
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was enacted in **1919** during the tenure of **Lord Chelmsford**.
 
• It gave the British government extraordinary powers to suppress political activities and detain individuals without trial.
 
• The act was widely opposed by Indian leaders and led to the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** in the same year.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: India's first National Park, the Hailey National Park, is better known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jim Corbett National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jim Corbett National Park**, formerly known as the **Hailey National Park**, was established in **1936**. It is located in the **Nainital district** of **Uttarakhand, India**.
 
• It was the **first national park** of India, marking the beginning of wildlife conservation in the country. *Hence, it is the correct answer.*
 
• The park was renamed after **Jim Corbett**, a famous hunter-turned-conservationist, who played a vital role in its establishment and in raising awareness about the importance of wildlife conservation.
 
• Jim Corbett National Park is part of the **Corbett Tiger Reserve** and is renowned for its successful implementation of **Project Tiger**, which was launched in **1973** for the conservation of the Bengal tiger.
 
• The park covers an area of approximately **520 square kilometers** and is known for its diverse flora and fauna, including species like Bengal tigers, leopards, elephants, and various bird species.
 
• Its terrain is a mix of hills, riverine belts, marshy depressions, grasslands, and a large lake, making it one of the most scenic national parks in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other National Parks Mentioned:**

 
 
• **Kaziranga National Park**: Located in **Assam**, it is famous for its population of the **one-horned rhinoceros**. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1985**.
 
• **Singalila National Park**: Situated in **West Bengal**, it is known for its **red panda population** and the breathtaking views of the Himalayan range.
 
• **Tadoba National Park**: Located in **Maharashtra**, it is one of the oldest and largest national parks in the state and is part of the **Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve**.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched in **1973**, Project Tiger aims to ensure the survival and growth of the tiger population in India. Jim Corbett National Park was the first park to be included under this project.
 
 
 
• **Jim Corbett's Legacy:**
 
 
• Jim Corbett was a British-Indian hunter and conservationist who wrote extensively about wildlife. His books, such as **"Man-Eaters of Kumaon"**, are widely regarded as classics in wildlife literature.
 
• He advocated for the protection of wildlife and forests, which ultimately led to the establishment of the Hailey National Park.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of National Parks:**

 
 
• National parks play a critical role in **conserving biodiversity**, protecting endangered species, and maintaining ecological balance.
 
• They also serve as important research and education centers, promoting awareness about wildlife and the environment.
 
 
 
• **Tourism:**
 
 
• Jim Corbett National Park is a popular tourist destination, attracting nature enthusiasts and wildlife photographers from across the globe.
 
• Tourism in the park is carefully regulated to minimize its impact on the environment while generating revenue for conservation efforts.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Son River:

 
• It is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga.
 
• It flows through southern Bihar.
 
• It originates in the Aravalli hills.

Which are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The Son River is indeed a **right-bank tributary of the Ganga River**. It joins the Ganga near Patna, Bihar, and flows parallel to the Ganga for a significant stretch before merging. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** The Son River flows through **southern Bihar**, which is one of the key regions in its course. It originates in Madhya Pradesh and passes through Jharkhand and southern Bihar before joining the Ganga. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3:** The claim that the Son River originates in the **Aravalli Hills** is incorrect. The Son River originates in the **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh. The Aravalli Hills are located in Rajasthan and Gujarat, which is geographically far from the Son River basin. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• *Thus, the correct answer is **1 and 2 only.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Son River Overview:**

 
 
• The Son River is one of the largest tributaries of the Ganga River and flows primarily through **Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar**.
 
• It originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau**, which is also the source of the Narmada River.
 
• The Son River is known for its wide and rocky bed and has limited water flow during non-monsoon months.
 
 
 
• **Geography of the Amarkantak Plateau:**
 
 
• The Amarkantak Plateau is located in **Madhya Pradesh**, near the border of Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is a significant geographical region as it serves as the origin of two major rivers: the **Narmada River** and the Son River.
 
• The plateau is rich in biodiversity and is considered sacred in Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Tributary Systems of the Ganga River:**
 
 
• The Ganga River has several tributaries, categorized as **left-bank and right-bank tributaries**.
 
• Examples of right-bank tributaries include the **Yamuna, Son, and Damodar Rivers**.
 
• Left-bank tributaries include the **Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi Rivers**.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Hills:**
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills are located in **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, and Delhi**.
 
• They are among the oldest mountain ranges in India and are geologically distinct from the regions where the Son River flows.
 
• The hills are known for their **mineral wealth** and **dry deciduous forests**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Son River's Significance:**

 
 
• The Son River basin supports agriculture in the regions through which it flows, particularly in **Bihar**.
 
• It has several dams and canals built for irrigation, such as the **Bansagar Dam**.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River System:**
 
 
• The Ganga River is one of the most important rivers in India and serves as the lifeline for millions of people.
 
• Its tributaries play a crucial role in sustaining ecosystems and livelihoods across northern and eastern India.

questions.question: Who is empowered to set up an Inter-State Council?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Inter-State Council** is established under **Article 263** of the **Constitution of India**. This article empowers the **President** to create such a council if it is deemed necessary.

• The council is intended to improve coordination between states and the central government on matters of common interest.

• The President establishes the council after consulting with state governments, ensuring the council addresses specific issues of inter-state or federal interest.

• The council provides a platform for dialogue on policies and disputes between states, aiming to ensure harmonious relationships within the federal structure of India.

• The **Sarkaria Commission**, set up in 1983 to review center-state relations, recommended the establishment of the Inter-State Council for better coordination and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Article 263 of the Constitution:** 

• It empowers the President to define the duties and functions of the Inter-State Council.

• The article specifies that the council may inquire and advise on disputes between states, discuss subjects of common interest, and make recommendations for better policy coordination.

• **Sarkaria Commission Recommendations:** 

• The Sarkaria Commission emphasized the need for institutional mechanisms to address issues between the center and states.

• It recommended the establishment of the Inter-State Council as a permanent constitutional body.

• **Current Status:** 

• The Inter-State Council was set up in **1990** by then Prime Minister **Vishwanath Pratap Singh**.

• It operates as a platform for states and the central government to collaborate on policies, resolve disputes, and ensure uniformity in governance.

• **Significance:** 

• The council promotes cooperative federalism and strengthens the relationship between the center and states.

• It plays a crucial role in resolving inter-state disputes and ensuring smooth administrative functioning across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Legal Framework:** The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263, unlike other advisory bodies or commissions formed by executive orders.

• **Composition:** The council includes the Prime Minister as the chairman, Chief Ministers of states, union ministers, and administrators of union territories.

• **Functions:** It advises on disputes between states, discusses subjects of common interest, and recommends better coordination of policy and action.

• **Historical Usage:** Although established in 1990, its meetings and effectiveness have varied over time, depending on political and administrative priorities.
</ul

questions.question:
In microeconomic theory, the Law of Supply explains the relationship between the price of a commodity and the quantity producers are willing to offer for sale, assuming other determinants remain unchanged.

Which one of the following statements best reflects the implication of the Law of Supply?

options.text: The quantity supplied of a commodity tends to rise when its market price increases.
The quantity supplied of a commodity tends to decline when its market price increases.
The quantity supplied of a commodity increases as consumer income rises.
The quantity supplied of a commodity decreases when consumer income increases.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option A. **

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Supply** is a fundamental principle of **microeconomics** which states that, **other things remaining constant (ceteris paribus)**, the **quantity supplied of a commodity increases when its price increases and decreases when its price decreases**.
 
• This occurs because **higher prices provide greater profit incentives to producers**, encouraging them to increase production and bring more goods to the market.
 
• Conversely, **lower prices reduce profitability**, leading producers to reduce the quantity supplied.
 
• Option A states that **the quantity supplied of a commodity tends to rise when its market price increases**, which correctly reflects the **direct relationship between price and supply** described by the Law of Supply. Hence, **the statement is correct. **
 
• Option B suggests that **quantity supplied declines when price increases**, which contradicts the basic principle of the Law of Supply.Hence, **the statement is incorrect. **
 
• Option C links **supply with consumer income**, which is a determinant of **demand rather than supply**. Hence, **the statement is incorrect. **
 
• Option D also relates **consumer income with supply**, which does not represent the Law of Supply. Hence, **the statement is incorrect. **

Thus, **the Law of Supply implies that quantity supplied increases when price increases → Option A. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ceteris Paribus Assumption:** The Law of Supply holds when other factors such as **technology, input prices, taxes, subsidies, and number of sellers remain constant**.
 
• **Supply Curve:** The relationship between **price and quantity supplied is represented by an upward-sloping supply curve** in standard microeconomic analysis.

**Movement vs Shift: **

 
• **Movement along the supply curve** occurs due to **changes in price**.
 
• **Shift of the supply curve** occurs due to factors like **technology changes, input costs, taxes/subsidies, expectations, or number of producers**.
 
• **Determinants of Supply:** Key determinants include **cost of production, technological progress, government policies, expectations of future prices, prices of related goods, and number of sellers in the market**.
 
• **Elasticity of Supply:** The responsiveness of quantity supplied to price changes is measured by **Price Elasticity of Supply**.
 
• **Exceptions / Special Cases:** In the **very short run (especially agriculture)** supply may be relatively fixed; also, producers may **withhold supply if they expect higher prices in the future**.
 
• **Relevance in Policy:** Understanding supply behaviour is important for **price policy, agricultural procurement, market regulation, and production incentives** in an economy.

questions.question: Who used the term "Quasi-federal" to characterize Indian Federal ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KC Wheare**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Ecotones are often described as “zones of tension” in ecology because:

options.text: They represent areas where environmental conditions are too harsh to support most life forms
They occur at the interface of two ecosystems, creating transitional conditions that lead to competition, stress, and adaptive pressures
They consistently exhibit lower species diversity than the ecosystems they separate
They are formed exclusively due to human activities such as agriculture and urban expansion.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option B**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In ecology, an **ecotone** is a **transitional zone** between two adjacent ecosystems (for example, forest–grassland or terrestrial–aquatic boundaries).
 
• Ecotones are described as **“zones of tension”** because organisms in these areas experience **overlapping environmental conditions**, leading to **competition, ecological stress, and strong adaptive pressures**. Hence, **Option B is correct**.
 
• Such zones often support **greater species diversity** due to the **edge effect**, not lower diversity. Hence, **Option C is incorrect**.
 
• Ecotones are **natural ecological features**, though they can also be influenced by human activities; they are **not formed exclusively by human actions**. Hence, **Option D is incorrect**.
 
• Harsh conditions alone do not define ecotones; rather, it is the **interaction of two ecosystems** that creates their distinctive characteristics. Hence, **Option A is incorrect**.
 
• [IMAGE: https://pmfias.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/ecotone-wetland.jpeg] 

 
• **Thus, the correct answer is → Option B. **

• The **edge effect** often results in **higher species richness** in ecotones compared to adjoining ecosystems.
 
• Ecotones can be **dynamic**, shifting in location due to climate change or land-use alterations.
 
• Examples include **estuaries, mangroves, forest–grassland boundaries, and alpine treelines**.

questions.question: Isochrone lines on a map connect places having equal:
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is:** "Travel time"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isochrone Lines:**

 
 
• Isochrone lines on a map connect points where the travel time to a specific location is equal.
 
• These lines are used to analyze accessibility and mobility from a given point, typically considering factors such as transport modes and road conditions.
 
• Isochrone maps are widely used in urban planning, transportation studies, and geographic analysis to assess how far one can travel within a certain time frame.
 
 
 
• **(Physical distance): **
 
 
• Isochrone lines are not related to physical distance. Instead, they represent accessibility based on time, which may vary depending on transport networks and traffic conditions.
 
• For example, two locations at the same physical distance from a point may have different travel times due to differences in road quality or congestion.
 
 
 
• **(Transport cost): **
 
 
• Transport cost is not a factor in creating isochrone lines. Isochrones solely focus on travel time, regardless of cost.
 
• Cost analysis is a separate concept often studied in economic geography or transport economics.
 
 
 
• **(Road length): **
 
 
• Isochrone lines do not represent road length; they represent time taken to travel, which depends on factors like speed limits, traffic, and transport modes, not just the length of the road.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Isochrone Maps:**
 
 
• Used in urban planning to understand accessibility to essential services like hospitals, schools, and public transportation.
 
• Helpful in transportation modeling to plan routes, assess congestion, or optimize travel time.
 
• Used by businesses to determine service areas and customer accessibility within a specific time frame.
 
• Aid in emergency response planning by identifying areas that can be reached within a certain time during crises.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isochrone Map Creation:**

 
 
• Isochrone maps are created using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) tools. These tools calculate travel time based on input data such as road networks, speed limits, and traffic conditions.
 
• They can also factor in different modes of transport, such as walking, driving, or public transit, to produce accurate representations.
 
 
 
• **Historical Use:**
 
 
• The concept of isochrone mapping dates back to the early 20th century and has evolved significantly with advancements in GIS technologies.
 
• Initially used for railway planning, the method has expanded to encompass multi-modal transport analysis.
 
 
 
• **Related Concepts:**
 
 
• **Isodistance Maps:** These maps connect points at the same physical distance from a central location, differing from isochrone maps which focus on time.
 
• **Network Analysis:** Isochrone mapping is a type of network analysis in GIS, focusing on accessibility within a given network.

questions.question: In macroeconomic analysis, the phenomenon of “crowding out” is best understood as which of the following situations?

options.text: Increased government borrowing leads to reduced availability of funds for private investment
Expansion of public expenditure results in higher private investment through multiplier effects
Reduction in interest rates encourages both public and private sector investment
Private sector borrowing reduces government expenditure.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• “**Crowding out**” refers to a situation where **increased government borrowing** (to finance fiscal deficits) leads to **reduced availability of funds for the private sector**.
 
• **When the government borrows heavily:** • It raises **demand for loanable funds ** • This pushes **interest rates upward ** • Higher interest rates **discourage private investment . **Hence, **Option A is correct. **
 
• **Option B** describes **crowding-in effect**, not crowding out. Hence, **incorrect**.
 
• **Option C** refers to a general **monetary easing condition**, not crowding out.** Hence, incorrect. **
 
• **Option D** does not represent the concept of crowding out. **Hence, incorrect. **
 
• Thus, **crowding out = government borrowing reduces private investment → Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Crowding Out: ****Financial crowding out:** Government borrowing raises **interest rates**, reducing private investment • **Resource crowding out:** Government uses **real resources (labour, capital)**, leaving fewer for private sector
 
• **Channels through which crowding out occurs: ** • **Interest rate channel** → higher borrowing cost • **Credit channel** → limited availability of loans • **Exchange rate channel** → capital inflows → currency appreciation → exports become less competitive
 
• **When crowding out is stronger: ** • Economy is at or near **full employment ** • **Limited savings pool** in the economy • **Tight monetary policy** (central bank not accommodating borrowing)
 
• **When crowding out is weaker or absent: ** • During **recession or demand slowdown ** • When there is **excess liquidity in banking system ** • When central bank follows **accommodative policy (monetisation of deficit) **
 
• **Crowding In vs Crowding Out: ** • **Crowding out:** Public borrowing reduces private investment • **Crowding in:** Public spending (e.g., infrastructure) **stimulates private investment **
 
• **Indian Context: ** • High fiscal deficits can raise concerns about **crowding out private investment ** • However, strong public capital expenditure (infrastructure) can also lead to **crowding-in effects.**

questions.question: Select the correct property of micelles in soap that help them to interact with water:

options.text: both hydrophilic head and hydrophobhic tail

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrophilic head**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Micelles** are tiny spherical structures formed by soap molecules in water. They are formed when the soap concentration in water crosses a critical micelle concentration.
 
• Each soap molecule has two distinct parts: a **hydrophobic tail** (water-repelling) and a **hydrophilic head** (water-attracting).
 
• The **hydrophilic head**__ of the soap molecule interacts with water molecules because it is polar in nature, allowing micelles to remain suspended in water.
 
• When soap is added to water, its **hydrophobic tail avoids water** and clusters together, while the **hydrophilic head faces outward, interacting with water**. This arrangement creates a stable micelle structure.
 
• The ability of micelles to interact with water and trap oily dirt is attributed to the polar nature of the __**hydrophilic head**__, which forms a strong interaction with water molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Soap Molecules:**

 
 
• Soap molecules are composed of a long hydrocarbon chain (hydrophobic tail) and a carboxylate ion (hydrophilic head).
 
• The hydrophobic tail is nonpolar and repels water, while the hydrophilic head is polar and interacts with water molecules.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Micelles:**
 
 
• When soap is added to water, the molecules arrange themselves in a spherical structure called a micelle.
 
• In a micelle, the hydrophilic heads face outward toward the water, and the hydrophobic tails cluster inward, avoiding water.
 
 
 
• **Cleaning Action of Soap:**
 
 
• The hydrophobic tail attaches to oily dirt, while the hydrophilic head remains in contact with water.
 
• This action forms an emulsion, breaking down the grease into smaller droplets that can be washed away with water.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hydrophilic Head:**
 
 
• The hydrophilic head ensures that soap molecules remain dispersed in water, preventing the micelles from aggregating and settling at the bottom.
 
• It also helps in the removal of dirt by solubilizing it into water.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Micelles:**
 
 
• Micelles are widely used in cleaning, emulsification, and even in drug delivery systems in pharmaceuticals.
 
• Their unique structure allows them to trap hydrophobic substances like oils and grease and interact with water simultaneously.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The hydrophobic tail is made of a long hydrocarbon chain, which repels water.
 
• It plays a critical role in trapping grease and oil but does not interact directly with water.
 
 
 
• **Hydrophilic Head:**
 
 
• The hydrophilic head is ionic or polar in nature, allowing it to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
 
• This property is crucial for the formation of micelles and their interaction with water.
 
 
 
• **Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC):**
 
 
• Micelles form only when the concentration of soap in water exceeds a certain threshold known as the Critical Micelle Concentration.
 
• Below this concentration, soap molecules remain dispersed and do not form micelles.

questions.question: The need for banks to keep some reserves in liquid form in the short term, is called which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statutory Liquid Ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Statutory Liquid Ratio (SLR) is the mandatory percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) to be maintained in liquid assets like cash, gold, or government-approved securities before offering credit to customers.
 
• SLR is a regulatory requirement imposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
 
• The primary purpose of SLR is to ensure the solvency of banks and control credit expansion, thereby maintaining the liquidity in the economy.
 
• Maintaining the SLR helps banks manage funds effectively and ensures that a certain portion of deposits is not used for high-risk investments.
 
• The SLR rate is periodically reviewed and adjusted by the RBI depending on the economic needs of the country.

• The CRR is the percentage of a bank's NDTL that must be kept as reserves in the form of cash with the RBI.
 
• It is used by the RBI to regulate liquidity and inflation in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate:**
 
 
• The rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks in the short term, generally against government securities.
 
• Changes in the repo rate directly influence the borrowing costs for banks and, consequently, the interest rates for consumers.
 
 
 
• **Bank Rate:**
 
 
• The rate at which the RBI lends long-term funds to commercial banks without requiring collateral.
 
• It is used to control money supply and stabilize the economy.
 
 
 
• **Importance of SLR:**
 
 
• It ensures that banks maintain a certain level of liquidity to meet unforeseen demands of depositors.
 
• It acts as a tool for monetary policy, helping the RBI regulate inflation and credit flow in the economy.

questions.question: The device used in submarines to give a clear view of the object on the surface of sea or land is known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Periscope**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• A **periscope** is a device used in submarines to allow the crew to observe objects on the surface of the water or land while the submarine remains submerged. 
• It works based on the principle of reflection of light using two or more mirrors or prisms arranged at a specific angle. 
• The periscope is designed to provide a clear line of sight above the water level, enabling the submarine to detect ships, aircraft, or other objects without surfacing. 
• Periscopes are not only used in submarines but also in tanks and other applications where direct line-of-sight observation is not possible. 
• The invention of the periscope revolutionized naval warfare by improving the stealth and safety of submarines during operations. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Working Principle of Periscope:** 
• The periscope uses two mirrors or prisms placed at a 45-degree angle to the line of sight. Light from the object enters the top mirror, gets reflected downwards, and then reflected again by the bottom mirror towards the observer’s eye. 
• This arrangement allows the observer to view objects that are not directly visible due to obstructions or the observer’s position. 
• **Applications of Periscope:** 
• Widely used in **submarines** for surface observations without surfacing. 
• Utilized in **tanks** to allow soldiers to view the battlefield while remaining protected inside the vehicle. 
• Used in certain **scientific instruments** and observational devices for specialized applications. 
• In some cases, periscopes are incorporated into **children’s toys** for educational purposes. 
• **Comparison with Similar Devices:** 
• **Sextant:** A navigational instrument used to measure the angle between two visible objects, primarily for celestial navigation. 
• **Stereoscope:** A device used to view two-dimensional images as three-dimensional by combining two slightly different perspectives. 
• **Telescope:** An optical device designed to observe distant objects by gathering and focusing light, commonly used in astronomy. 
• **Historical Background:** 
• The basic principle of the periscope has been known since ancient times, but modern designs were developed in the 19th and 20th centuries. 
• Sir Howard Grubb, an Irish engineer, significantly improved the periscope design for use in submarines during World War I. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Submarine Periscopes:** 
• Modern submarine periscopes often incorporate advanced technologies like **night vision**, **thermal imaging**, and **rangefinders**. 
• They are crucial for navigation, surveillance, and ensuring the safety of the submarine during operations. 
• **Limitations:** 
• Traditional periscopes have a limited field of view and range. 
• Advanced designs have addressed these limitations by incorporating digital cameras and electronic displays.

questions.question: Intense thunderstorms, marked by lightning, thunder, and heavy rainfall, are predominantly formed by which type of cloud?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cumulonimbus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cumulonimbus clouds** are large, towering clouds that are associated with severe weather phenomena like thunderstorms, lightning, and heavy rainfall.
 
• These clouds form due to the rapid upward movement of warm, moist air, which cools and condenses at higher altitudes, creating towering structures.
 
• Cumulonimbus clouds can reach altitudes of up to 12-20 kilometers and often have a characteristic anvil-shaped top caused by high-altitude winds spreading the cloud horizontally.
 
• They are known to produce extreme weather conditions, including hail, tornadoes, and flash floods, making them one of the most dangerous cloud types.
 
• These clouds are typically found in unstable atmospheric conditions, where warm air near the surface rises rapidly through cooler air above.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nimbostratus Clouds**

 
 
• Nimbostratus clouds are thick, uniform layers of gray clouds that cover the sky and are associated with steady, prolonged rainfall or snowfall rather than intense thunderstorms.
 
• These clouds are typically found in stable atmospheric conditions and do not produce lightning or thunder.
 
 
 
• **Cumulus Clouds**
 
 
• Cumulus clouds are puffy, white clouds with flat bases that often appear in fair weather conditions.
 
• While they can develop into cumulonimbus clouds under the right conditions, they are generally not associated with severe weather on their own.
 
 
 
• **Stratocumulus Clouds**
 
 
• Stratocumulus clouds are low-altitude clouds that appear as large, dark, rounded masses or rolls, often covering the sky in patches.
 
• These clouds typically produce light precipitation, such as drizzle, but are not linked to thunderstorms or intense rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Theme of the Question**
 
 
• Thunderstorms are intense weather phenomena caused by the rapid upward movement of warm, moist air, resulting in condensation and the formation of towering clouds.
 
• The type of cloud formed depends on atmospheric conditions, with cumulonimbus being the most common cloud type associated with severe thunderstorms.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of land reforms in India post independence?

options.text: To change in the ownership of landholdings.
To increase foreign direct investment in agriculture.
To sell all the landholdings to private companies for better compliance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To change in the ownership of landholdings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main purpose of land reforms in India post-independence was to bring about **equitable ownership of land** by redistributing land from large landholders to landless farmers and tenants.
 
• Land reforms aimed at addressing the issue of **concentration of land** in the hands of a few wealthy individuals, thereby reducing inequality and ensuring social justice.
 
• These reforms included measures like **abolition of zamindari system**, tenancy reforms, and ceilings on landholdings to prevent excessive accumulation of land by individuals. 
 
• The focus was on **empowering small and marginal farmers** and ensuring their access to agricultural land to improve their socio-economic conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Abolition of Zamindari System:**

 
 
• This was one of the earliest measures taken post-independence to eliminate the intermediary system of zamindars who collected revenue on behalf of the British.
 
• The **Zamindari Abolition Act** was implemented in various states to transfer ownership rights to the tillers of the land.
 
• It marked a significant step towards reducing feudal practices and empowering cultivators. 
 
 
 
• **Tenancy Reforms:**
 
 
• Tenancy reforms aimed at securing the rights of tenants by providing protection against arbitrary eviction and granting ownership rights in some cases.
 
• Measures like **fixation of fair rent** and **prohibition of subletting** were introduced to safeguard tenant farmers.
 
• In states like West Bengal and Kerala, tenancy reforms significantly improved the socio-economic status of tenant farmers. 
 
 
 
• **Ceilings on Landholdings:**
 
 
• Land ceiling laws were enacted to limit the maximum land an individual or family could own, and surplus land was redistributed among landless individuals.
 
• The surplus land was allocated to marginalized groups, including **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
• This policy aimed at reducing inequality and ensuring equitable distribution of resources. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• Land reforms were introduced as a part of India's social and economic policies post-independence to address the issues of rural poverty and inequality.
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)** emphasized land reforms as a key strategy for rural development. 
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• The **Ninth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution was introduced to safeguard land reform laws from judicial review.
 
• Articles like **Article 39(b) and (c)** of the Directive Principles of State Policy underline the importance of equitable distribution of resources.

questions.question: The planning in India was inspired largely by the planning system of ______.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: __USSR.__**

India's planning system was inspired by the model of centralized economic planning that the Soviet Union (USSR) adopted under its socialist framework. This approach aimed to achieve rapid industrialization, equitable distribution of resources, and comprehensive socio-economic development by setting long-term goals and implementing structured strategies through Five-Year Plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inspiration from the Soviet Model: **
 
 
• The USSR's planning system emphasized state-led development through centralized planning. India adopted a similar structure to achieve economic self-reliance and reduce dependence on foreign powers after gaining independence in 1947.
 
 
 
• **Establishment of the Planning Commission: **
 
 
• India established the Planning Commission in 1950 to formulate and oversee Five-Year Plans, a mechanism similar to the Soviet Union's planning approach.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Industrialization: **
 
 
• The Soviet model's emphasis on rapid industrialization was mirrored in India's plans. The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), for instance, prioritized heavy industries like steel, coal, and infrastructure to boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Dominance: **
 
 
• Much like the USSR, India adopted a mixed economy where the public sector played a dominant role in key industries, while the private sector was regulated to ensure equitable resource distribution.
 
 
 
• **Socialist Ideals: **
 
 
• India's planning approach reflected socialist ideals, aiming to reduce poverty, eliminate income disparities, and achieve social justice, aligning with the principles of the Soviet model.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of Indian Planning: **
 
 
• Adoption of Five-Year Plans to set specific development goals.
 
• Focus on self-reliance in agriculture, industry, and technology.
 
• Promotion of import substitution to reduce foreign dependency.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Soviet Influence: **
 
 
• Although India was inspired by the USSR, it adopted a mixed economy rather than a fully state-controlled system, allowing the private sector to coexist with the public sector.
 
• India retained democratic governance, unlike the Soviet Union's authoritarian regime.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Soviet-Inspired Planning: **
 
 
• India's early plans laid the foundation for its industrial and infrastructural development, contributing significantly to its economic progress.
 
• The planning system evolved over time, eventually transitioning to a more market-driven approach with the establishment of the NITI Aayog in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the plant hormones?

I. They help to coordinate growth, development and responses to the environment.

II. They are synthesised at places away from where they act and simply diffuse to the area of action
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plant hormones:** Plant hormones, also known as phytohormones, are chemical substances that significantly influence various physiological processes in plants, such as growth, development, and environmental responses.
 
• **Statement I:** "They help to coordinate growth, development, and responses to the environment" is **correct**. Plant hormones regulate processes like cell elongation, flowering, fruit ripening, and stress responses, ensuring plants adapt to changing environmental conditions.
 
• **Statement II:** "They are synthesized at places away from where they act and simply diffuse to the area of action" is **incorrect**. While some plant hormones like auxins are produced in specific regions (e.g., shoot tips) and transported to the target site, not all hormones follow this mechanism. Cytokinins, for example, are synthesized in roots and transported upward via xylem. The movement of hormones often involves active transport rather than simple diffusion.
 
• **Examples:** Auxins promote cell elongation, gibberellins regulate stem elongation, and ethylene controls fruit ripening. These demonstrate how plant hormones coordinate growth and environmental adaptations.
 
• **Correct Option:** Based on the explanation, only Statement I is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Plant Hormones:**

 
 
• **Auxins:** Promote cell elongation, apical dominance, and root initiation. Example: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA).
 
• **Gibberellins:** Stimulate stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering. Example: GA3.
 
• **Cytokinins:** Promote cell division and delay leaf senescence. Example: Zeatin.
 
• **Ethylene:** A gaseous hormone responsible for fruit ripening, flower wilting, and leaf abscission.
 
• **Abscisic Acid (ABA):** Induces dormancy and regulates stress responses like drought tolerance.
 
 
 
• **Plant Hormone Transport:**
 
 
• Hormones like auxins move via polar transport, whereas cytokinins are transported through vascular tissues.
 
• Active transport mechanisms involve specific proteins, ensuring hormones reach target sites effectively.
 
 
 
• **Key Functions:**
 
 
• **Growth regulation:** Hormones control cell division, elongation, and differentiation.
 
• **Environmental adaptation:** Hormones help plants respond to stress, light, and gravity.
 
• **Developmental processes:** They regulate flowering, fruiting, seed germination, and dormancy.
 
 
 
• **Examples in Agriculture:**
 
 
• **Auxins:** Used in rooting powders and herbicides.
 
• **Ethylene:** Utilized for artificial fruit ripening.
 
• **Gibberellins:** Applied to increase fruit size in crops like grapes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery:** Auxins were first discovered by Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin in their experiments on phototropism in canary grass.
 
• **Significance in Crop Improvement:** Genetic engineering of hormone pathways is used to enhance crop yield and stress tolerance.
 
• **Stress Hormones:** Abscisic Acid (ABA) is crucial for drought resistance, helping plants conserve water during adverse conditions.
 
• **Global Applications:** Plant hormones are integral to modern agricultural practices, including tissue culture and hybrid seed production.

• **Munda language group** belongs to the **Austro-Asiatic** language family.
 
• This language family is one of the **oldest groups of languages** spoken in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The Austro-Asiatic languages are primarily spoken in **Southeast Asia** and parts of **India**.
 
• In India, they are predominantly spoken by the **tribal communities** in regions like **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and West Bengal**.
 
• The **Munda languages** include several dialects such as **Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Korku**, and others.
 
• **Santhali**, a prominent language of the Munda group, was included in the **Eighth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution, granting it official recognition.
 
• The Austro-Asiatic language family is characterized by features such as **monosyllabic words** and the use of **prefixes** to indicate grammatical functions.
 
• The origin of the Austro-Asiatic languages is believed to be in the regions of **South China** and then later spread to **Southeast Asia** and India.
 
• These languages are significant in understanding the **cultural heritage** and **linguistic diversity** of tribal populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indo-Aryan**__

 __
 
• The **Indo-Aryan** language family is the largest language family in India and includes prominent languages such as **Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, and Urdu**.
 
• It is a subgroup of the **Indo-European language family** and is spoken by a majority of the Indian population.
 
• These languages have a significant presence in **North India** and parts of **Western and Eastern India**.
 
• Indo-Aryan languages are known for their rich **literary traditions** and contributions to **Indian culture**.
 
 
 
• **Sino-Tibetan**__
 __
 
• The **Sino-Tibetan** language family includes languages spoken in **Northeast India**, such as **Manipuri, Bodo, Mizo**, and other tribal languages.
 
• This group is primarily distributed across **China, Tibet, Northeast India, and Southeast Asia**.
 
• Sino-Tibetan languages are known for their **tonal features**, where pitch is used to distinguish word meanings.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian**__
 
 
• The **Dravidian** language family is native to **South India** and includes languages such as **Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam**, and **Tulu**.
 
• It is one of the **oldest language families in the world**, with roots tracing back to the **Indus Valley Civilization**.
 
• Dravidian languages are characterized by their **agglutinative structure**, where words are formed by combining morphemes.
